reader.requirement: At --std 85 a START with KEY phrase (EQUAL/=, GREATER/>, NOT LESS/NOT <, GREATER OR EQUAL/>=, the only 1985 operators) must compare, in the file's (native) collating sequence on the ascending key of reference, each record's key against data-name-1 (or the prime RECORD KEY item when the phrase is omitted), truncating the longer operand on the right to the shorter (generic alphanumeric key), set the file position indicator to the key-of-reference value of the first record satisfying it, and raise the invalid key condition (status 23) when no record satisfies it.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the reverse-search operators (LESS, <, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL) below COBOL-2002 (COBOL0900); the 1985 forward set passes
InForce (Edition.Year < 2002): the 1985 mandatory INVALID KEY / USE requirement (SR3), not GR4
ctx.Edition.SubscriptedClauseOperands gates the OCCURS screen on data-name-1 (operand shape, not the comparison)

reader.edition-search: Read BindStart, EmitStart, IndexedConnector.Start/KeyOf/StartSucceeded and ResolveKeyCollating; the comparison itself (Seek with prefix over compareLength = data-name-1's width, native order absent a 2002+ file COLLATING SEQUENCE clause) consults no edition: the 85 arm is the 2023 arm.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the admitted operator set (1985 has no LESS / NOT GREATER / LESS OR EQUAL, and no WITH LENGTH or FIRST/LAST); the comparison, truncation and invalid-key outcome are one code path.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness pb358 exercises the omitted KEY phrase (implied EQUAL on the prime key) and explicit >=; it does not exercise >, NOT LESS, the generic (shorter) operand's truncation, alternate keys with duplicates, or a record description other than the key's.

reader.notes: The runtime slices the key of reference out of the record area for data-name-1's width (the 2023 GR17a model); at 1985 data-name-1 is required (SR4) to lie in a record of the file at the key's leftmost position, so the area bytes are data-name-1's bytes and the two models agree. All probed operators, generic truncation, alternate duplicate keys and the no-match invalid key behave as GR4 states.
